name: Rafael Nuñez International Airport
before:
Cartagena's airport, and the largest in Colombia's northern Caribbean region by passenger numbers. It sits in the Crespo neighbourhood in the north of the city, between the Caribbean coast and the Ciénaga de la Virgen marsh, which makes for an unusually short run into town.

The route map is wide for a regional airport. American, JetBlue, Avianca, Copa, LATAM, Wingo, EasyFly, Air Panama and Air Transat have flown international services to North, Central and South America, and KLM and Edelweiss serve Amsterdam and Zurich by way of Bogotá, though neither airline can carry a passenger only between Cartagena and Bogotá.

The runway is 2,600 metres by 60 at sea level, which is enough for modern transatlantic aircraft, and there is parking for eleven aircraft.

OINAC has held a ten year contract to run and expand the airport since March 2024.

It is named after Rafael Núñez, a Cartagena native who was president of Colombia and wrote the words to the national anthem.
after:
Cartagena's airport sits beside the Crespo neighbourhood in the north of the city, a short run from the centre. It handled more than 7.7 million passengers in 2025, a record, according to its operator, OINAC.

The route map is wide for a regional airport. International flights reach North, Central and South America, among them American Airlines from Miami. KLM flies to Amsterdam on a route that also calls at Bogotá, and Edelweiss runs a seasonal Zurich service the same way.

The runway is 2,600 metres long and at sea level, which is enough for modern transatlantic aircraft.

OINAC took over the airport in early 2024 under a concession to expand it, and modernisation works, which include a new international terminal, are under way.

It is named after Rafael Núñez.

claims.note: ANI, the national infrastructure agency, and OINAC signed the start of the new concession on 29 February 2024, when SACSA, which had run the airport since 1996, handed it back (ANI's release, as published on the operator's site); Wikipedia says 1 March 2024. 'Early 2024' is what both support. Aviacionline (19 August 2026) confirms OINAC as the current concession holder.

claims.claim: use the airport's authorised taxi stations
claims.why: Held back: the operator has two authorised taxi stations, at the domestic and international exits, and recommends passengers always use them; the FCDO says there are authorised taxi booths at most Colombian airports and warns of robberies in unlicensed taxis. The operator's FAQ adds that Transcaribe's trunk route T102 (Portal to Crespo) runs past the airport. Useful, but nothing in the old text to replace. For Andy to decide.
